purpose: Define which authoritative baseline and caveats apply to each displayed market size system.

globalBaseline.warning: ISO 19407 describes approximate cross-system guidance, not a universal brand-fit guarantee.

markets.rule: Express the intended foot length in millimetres; optional foot width may follow.

markets.relationship: National adoption with international kinship to ISO 19407:2023

markets.caveat: No separate current DIN national adoption was confirmed in this research. Do not label the EU conversion as a DIN rule.
The official UNI catalogue entry found is ISO 19407, not a separate Italian size-conversion formula.

markets.relationship: Based on ISO 9407:1991 with additional Japanese provisions
markets.rule: Japanese shoe size is based on foot length together with ball girth or foot width; length is normally displayed in centimetres.
markets.appCaveat: Do not treat a JP length-only result as a complete fit recommendation when width/girth is unknown.

markets.rule: Use the same millimetre foot-length number as Mondopoint.

markets.authorityFinding: NIST defines shoe size as the manufacturer-designated size and states there is no strict dimensional relationship between a manufacturer's shoe size and outsole length or width.
markets.appRule: Use ISO 19407 as the generic baseline and permit brand-specific overrides.

markets.standard: No current national consumer shoe-size conversion standard confirmed
markets.appRule: If AU/NZ is offered, label it as a market convention and map to UK only as an approximate default; allow brand overrides.
markets.caveat: AS/NZS footwear standards found concern protective-footwear selection and fit, not a universal consumer conversion table.

implementationRules: Store foot length in millimetres as the canonical input and conversion pivot.
Separate standard conversion results from brand-specific label results.
Show Standard estimate or Brand chart as the result provenance.
Never infer width, ball girth, shoe volume or toe-box fit from length alone.
For Japan, support an optional width or girth field in a later version.
For US and AU/NZ, disclose that the result is approximate and may vary by manufacturer.
Do not describe EU sizes as one legally harmonized EU consumer sizing standard.
